rows.title: Meet the Colorado couple trying to make sure the art — yes, art — of broom-making isn’t swept away
rows.standfirst: At their quaint shop in Victor, Karen and Sam Morrison use century-old tools and techniques to craft their sought-after wares

rows.title: Health insurer Friday Health Plans goes under, leaving 30,000 Coloradans needing to find new coverage next year
rows.standfirst: Friday Health Plans’ announcement comes after it hit regulatory turmoil in Texas and other states

rows.title: Seven Peaks music festival won’t return to Colorado’s San Luis Valley
rows.standfirst: The three-day country music Seven Peaks festival started in 2019 in Buena Vista and moved to Villa Grove last year. Founder Dierks Bentley said it could move to Red Rocks this year.

rows.title: An electric bike leasing program is coming to low-income communities in Colorado Springs
rows.standfirst: An e-bike will be made available to 50 low-income people in Colorado Springs starting in July. The Colorado Energy Office provided funding for a leasing program.

rows.title: What’s Working: Where a company that develops cancer tests, other startups are finding funding in Colorado
rows.standfirst: It’s the state’s Advanced Industries program, which has provided $128 million in grants to early-stage companies in the past decade. So, what do taxpayers get out of it?

rows.title: Colorado governor vetoes bill that would have given local governments right of first refusal to buy multifamily housing
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1190 was aimed at increasing affordable housing options across the state. Business groups asked Gov. Jared Polis to veto it. The measure’s Democratic sponsors are furious.

rows.title: Why a showdown over Jared Polis’ big health insurance reform program fizzled — and what it means
rows.standfirst: Public hearings over prices for Colorado Option plans were supposed to kick off this week, but the first one was canceled

rows.title: Planning for the inevitable in Buena Vista, residents offer ideas for community development at The Meadows
rows.standfirst: There’s a 277-acre slice of undisturbed pasture on the west edge of Buena Vista, with 14er views, senior water rights and old farm roads. After a decade of events, the Selby family asked for public opinion on its New Urban future.

rows.title: Jared Polis signs bill prohibiting growth caps, repealing existing ones in Lakewood, Golden and Boulder
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1255 was intended to be a companion to the governor’s land-use measure, which Democrats failed to pass

rows.title: Why could Montana Republicans reshape land use but Colorado Democrats couldn’t?
rows.standfirst: Montana’s legislature this year passed laws restricting bans on accessory dwelling units, encouraging construction of duplexes and requiring cities to adopt strategies to increase housing

rows.title: Developers behind San Luis Valley water export plan pour money into Douglas County water district races
rows.standfirst: Two candidates for Parker water board received large campaign contributions from group wanting to build a $400 million pipeline to siphon water from southern Colorado

rows.title: Vail Resorts declines voluntary recognition of Crested Butte lift mechanics union, forcing a formal election
rows.standfirst: Crested Butte Mountain Resort ski patrollers were among the first to form a union in the 1970s. Now the ski area’s lift crew is seeking to unionize as part of a resort labor renaissance

rows.title: Consumer focus at Big Gear show in Denver is “the seed” for a new SXSW-style outdoors festival in Colorado
rows.standfirst: Visit Denver, the Colorado Outdoor Recreation Industry Office and Outside, Inc. teaming up at the Big Gear Show as first step toward a possible statewide outdoors festival

rows.title: Denver judge rejects effort to block 10-year property tax relief plan from going before Colorado voters in November
rows.standfirst: Denver District Court Judge David H. Goldberg rejected arguments that Proposition HH violates requirements in the state constitution that ballot measures deal with a single subject and have clear titles

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s summer jobs are disappearing
rows.standfirst: Fewer teenagers are part of Colorado’s labor force than past decades. Employers are focusing on retention and hiring longer-term workers.

rows.title: CPW slashed hunting licenses to save wildlife. What about Colorado towns that rely on hunters?
rows.standfirst: Thousands fewer tags and shorter seasons means thousands fewer hunters and a lot less spending in towns like Craig, Meeker and Rangely

rows.title: Colorado-based company accused of cultural appropriation over Native-inspired designs, products
rows.standfirst: Astis Mittens sees backlash over its Indigenous designs, says it’s working to hire Native artists

rows.title: Side-by-side photos show how much Blue Mesa Reservoir’s water levels have risen thanks to this winter’s snow
rows.standfirst: Pictures document “Big Blue” in 2021 and again in 2023

rows.title: Kamala Harris urges students to take action on climate change in Denver speech
rows.standfirst: The vice president gave brief remarks from a Denver high school before attending a campaign fundraising event

rows.title: What’s Working: Connecting Colorado’s latest economic reports on inflation, housing and jobs
rows.standfirst: Denver inflation falls but is still higher than the nation. Plus: Housing prices dip, more Coloradans are working and wages are growing. But slower.

rows.title: Colorado ski resorts enjoyed a record season with mountain towns harvesting highest-ever tax revenue
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s 27 lift-served ski areas saw a record 14.8 million visits in 2022-23, marking an 18% increase over the five-year average

rows.title: A proposal to put three warehouses beside a beloved JeffCo lake is Colorado’s latest land-use battle
rows.standfirst: Hundreds of homeowners are fighting a developer’s plan to build warehouses next to Hyatt Lake, just outside the town limits of Arvada

rows.title: A Colorado program is training the next generation of outdoor innovators
rows.standfirst: Western Colorado University is becoming an institutional hub for the outdoor recreation industry and the Gunnison River Valley as a hotbed for outdoor businesses

rows.title: Colorado taxpayers will get even larger refund checks next year than predicted. Here’s how much you can expect.
rows.standfirst: The TABOR surplus is now estimated at more than $3 billion, up to $800 million more than state economists predicted in March

rows.title: From hijabs to collapsible baby bottles, Denver’s Big Gear Show makes move toward inclusivity
rows.standfirst: There were times when Natalia Ospina felt as if she had to pick between her beloved outdoors and her hair. The Denver resident loved climbing and trail running. But she loved her hair, too. It reminded her of her mother, the only other one in her large family who had the same thick, luxurious curls […]

rows.title: What’s Working: What happened since Colorado invested in Colorado Springs as a cybersecurity hub
rows.standfirst: The city had a big head start with five nearby military bases. Now the region’s cybersecurity growth is on the map and ahead of metro areas like Denver.

rows.title: A group of Denver renters are fed up with rising rents and bad conditions. So they crashed a party for landlords.
rows.standfirst: About 100 residents, joined by Colorado Homes for All, protested Thursday outside the Apartment Association of Metro Denver awards ceremony. Six went in and walked onto the stage

rows.title: Modular housing community near Telluride that may become a Colorado model welcomes its first residents after months of delays
rows.standfirst: A new modular home community in Norwood creates a model for affordable housing in mountain communities with donated land, low-interest loans.

rows.title: Workers at several Colorado Starbucks stores join nationwide strike as company, unions remain at odds
rows.standfirst: Monday’s one-day strike was meant to draw attention to LGBTQ+ causes and a lack of progress in contract negotiations

rows.title: Colorado awarded $826.5 million from Biden administration to get everyone in the state decent broadband
rows.standfirst: The money, part of the federal Infrastructure Act of 2021, was more than state officials expected. It’s enough to get 99% of households to “adequate” internet service.

rows.title: Jim Crown, “a force of nature,” pushed Aspen Skiing Co. to lead on climate and sustainability
rows.standfirst: Resort industry reeling after Crown’s death driving a racecar on a track near Aspen on his 70th birthday

rows.title: Resort operator turns to Colorado Mountain College to train much-needed next generation of lift mechanics
rows.standfirst: The company, whose resorts include Steamboat, partnered with Colorado Mountain College to get lift mechanics swiftly trained in the cornerstone job of all ski resorts

rows.title: Colorado has lofty goals to go all-electric. But does the state have enough electricians?
rows.standfirst: As federal and state incentives kick in, industry experts fear there aren’t enough skilled electricians to help meet the demand for EV chargers and heat pumps

rows.title: Jared Polis, Western governors push geothermal energy development during Boulder conference
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s governor chose geothermal exploration as his top focus when he was voted chair of the Western Governors’ Association in 2022. A year on, a new report reveals the potential is hot.

rows.title: Colorado rides cresting wave of psychedelic medicine as state prepares to roll out regulation
rows.standfirst: The Psychedelic Science 2023 conference in Denver was the largest-ever gathering of psychedelic scientists, researchers, medical professionals, policy makers and entrepreneurs
